b.answer:
Worked example: the playground's three Harvest Lane items, in a test scenario.

#ModuleSettings
1JSON · Parse JSONJSON string: the items array wrapped as {"items": [ … ]}; data structure generated from that sample
2Flow control · IteratorArray: 1.items
3Tools · Text aggregatorSource module: 2. Iterator; Text: {{2.qty}}× {{2.name}} · ₦{{formatNumber(2.qty * 2.unit_price; 0; "."; ",")}}; Row separator: new line
4Gmail · Send an EmailTo: your own address; Subject: Order items (test); Content: 3.text

The email you receive (one only):

2× Tomatoes · ₦25,000
1× Tatashe · ₦9,000
3× Onions · ₦12,000

Bubble counts after Run once: Parse JSON 1 · Iterator 3 · Text aggregator 1 · Gmail 1. If Gmail shows 3, it is inside the iterated section: move it after the aggregator.
mistakes: Leaving the text aggregator's source module on Parse JSON, so the bundle counts look wrong.
Placing the Gmail module between the iterator and aggregator, which sends three emails.
Feeding the iterator text instead of the parsed array, so it outputs one bundle.
Calculating the line total as a string with ₦ before multiplying.
b.pass: The run's bubble counts show Iterator 3 and Text aggregator 1, and exactly one email arrives listing all three items with correct line totals (₦25,000, ₦9,000, ₦12,000).
b.redo: Send it back if more than one email arrives, if the counts aren't shown, or if any line total is wrong.

Worked example: Harvest Lane, five test orders, opening stock TOM-CRATE 40, PEP-TATASHE-L 20, ONI-BAG 30. Part A writes one Stock_Movements row per item and one confirmation per order; Part B sends the 18:00 summary.

ProductOpeningSold (hand count)ExpectedProducts sheet
TOM-CRATE4093131 ✓

Stock_Movements has 10 rows. HL-0102's two tomato lines are separate rows (−2 and −1), and the SUMIFS formula drops stock by exactly 3. Each order produced one confirmation email (text aggregator source = Iterator), five in total.

Part B email at 18:00: "Today: 5 orders · ₦180,000" followed by five lines like HL-0101 · Ade Bakare · ₦47,500. Numeric aggregators: SUM of total and COUNT, both with source module = the Search Rows module.

Submit: screenshots of Stock_Movements, Products, one confirmation and the summary email (test names only), plus the hand-count table.
mistakes: Overwriting stock_qty from inside the iterator, so the repeated-product order loses a crate.
Skipping the repeated-product or single-item test order.
Summing a ₦-formatted total in the numeric aggregator, so the day's sales show 0.
Setting the confirmation aggregator's source to the trigger, so one email lists items from several customers.
s.pass: Products stock matches a hand count for every SKU after five test orders (including a repeated product and a single item), each order got one confirmation, and the single summary shows the right count and naira total.
s.redo: Send it back if stock is off by any amount, if any customer got more or fewer than one confirmation, or if the summary count or total is wrong.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's Thursday 07:00 restock scenario. (If Order_Items has no date, add a created_at column when items are written.)

#ModuleSettings
1Sheets · Search RowsOrder_Items where created_at ≥ formatDate(addDays(now; -14); "YYYY-MM-DD")
2Numeric aggregatorSUM of qty · Group by: sku · Source: module 1
3Sheets · Search RowsProducts where sku = the group key (returns stock_qty)
Link filterWill run outstock_qty < round(2.result / 14 * 3) (Thursday to Saturday)
4Table aggregatorSource: module 2 · columns: product, stock, expected demand, suggested order
5GmailTo Tolu: "Restock before Saturday" + the table

Suggested order = ceil(expected * 1.2 - stock_qty), a 20% buffer for the Saturday rush.

Product14-day qtyStockExpected Thu–SatSuggested order
TOM-CRATE84121810
ONI-BAG42794

PEP-TATASHE-L (28 sold, stock 16, expected 6) is filtered out because it won't run out.

Manual check: a SUMIFS on Order_Items over the same 14 days gives 84 tomato crates and 42 onion bags, matching the aggregator. Lower TOM-CRATE stock to 12 in a test copy and tomatoes appear; raise it to 30 and they drop off the list.

Submit: the scenario screenshot, the email, and your manual SUMIFS check side by side.
mistakes: Forgetting Group by, so the aggregator gives one total for all products.
Comparing two weeks of demand with stock instead of the demand expected before Saturday.
A date filter that misses the time zone or uses mm for months, so the 14-day window is wrong.
No manual check, so a wrong total in the email is never noticed.
g.pass: The Thursday email lists product, stock, expected demand and suggested order quantity; the 14-day totals match a manual SUMIFS; and tomatoes appear when their stock is set low.
g.redo: Send it back if the totals don't match the sheet, if products with enough stock are listed, or if there is no evidence of a low-stock tomato test.
